OpenWrt DS-Lite (IPv4 over IPv6)

Why Japanese broadband commonly uses DS-Lite

The traditional method (PPPoE) queues at NTT’s network termination equipment (BRAS, responsible for PPPoE authentication and assigning IPv4),
and speeds drop severely during evening peak hours. The reason is that NTT’s BRAS expansion standard is calculated by number of connected users (sessions),
not by actual traffic: per-user traffic has increased more than tenfold, but if the session count has not reached the threshold, capacity is not expanded.
Who bears the expansion cost (NTT or the ISP) has also remained disputed, so this problem has dragged on for many years without being solved.

The workaround is to have ISPs build their own IPv6 networks (IPoE / v6plus, Xpass),
so traffic does not pass through the BRAS. But pure IPv6 cannot access IPv4 websites, so IPv4 packets are encapsulated in an IPv6 tunnel,
and decapsulated by the gateway on the ISP side (AFTR)—this is DS-Lite (RFC 6333).
Another similar scheme in Japan is MAP-E (JPNE/KDDI-affiliated), while DS-Lite is used by NTT-affiliated ISPs.

Cost: behind the AFTR is carrier-grade NAT (CGNAT), and home routers cannot get a public IPv4 address,
so port forwarding/self-hosted services require another approach (use IPv6 or NAT traversal).

OpenWrt Configuration

1. Install packages

After installation, restart LuCI or the router.

2. Create an interface

Network → Interfaces → Add new interface:

  • Name: dslite (fill in this name in the later traffic-splitting script)
  • Protocol: Dual-Stack Lite (RFC6333)
  • AFTR address: prefer an IPv6 address; do not enter a domain name

When entering a domain name (e.g. dgw.xpass.jp), the router must first resolve the AAAA record before it can establish the tunnel,
and this process depends on wan6’s DNS—if the connection has just been dialed and DNS is not ready yet, resolution fails,
so the DS-Lite interface remains unable to connect. Entering an IP directly skips this step.

ISPAFTR domainAFTR IPv6 address
Rakuten Hikari (Xpass)dgw.xpass.jp2001:f60:0:200::1:1
transix (IIJ, etc.)gw.transix.jpEast Japan 2404:8e00::feed:100, West Japan 2404:8e01::feed:100
v6 Connectdslite.v6connect.netObtained via DNS resolution

The IP is an address on the carrier side and may theoretically change; if you cannot connect, first use nslookup -type=AAAA dgw.xpass.jp
to confirm the current value (transix may not be found using public DNS; refer to the carrier’s announcement).

Other options:

  • The IPv6 interface on the WAN port (usually wan6) must first obtain an address starting with 240 before DS-Lite can establish the tunnel
  • Firewall zone: select wan
  • Advanced Settings → Use gateway metric: enter 10 (higher priority than backup lines such as apartment networks)

3. Coexist with PPPoE

When both lines are available at the same time, use the metric to set priority: enter 10 for DS-Lite and 20 for PPPoE.
Normally traffic goes through DS-Lite; if it goes down, it automatically falls back to PPPoE. To force a specific machine to use PPPoE, use policy routing; see “Interface Traffic Splitting”.

Automatic Failover on Disconnection

/root/failover.sh (cron: * * * * * /root/failover.sh),
if DS-Lite is unreachable, remove its default route, and traffic falls back to the backup line:

The same applies to the IPv6 side (/root/failover_v6.sh); fill in the interface name of the one that actually obtains an address starting with 240:

Pitfalls

  • Port forwarding cannot be used: behind the AFTR is CGNAT, with no public IPv4. To provide services externally, use IPv6.
  • The IPv4 of the DS-Lite interface is a carrier private address; do not use it for local service binding.
  • When you only get one /64 PD, subnets need NAT6 or relay; see “ipv6 nat” and “Assigning public v6 to subnets”.

References

  • Mechanism of DS-Lite - Geek Page
  • FLETS Hikari problem of becoming extremely slow at night will not be solved in the short term
  • Main issues in FLETS service speed degradation and the association’s measures - JAIPA
  • DS-Lite connection using OpenWrt - Qiita
  • Installing OpenWrt on a thousand-yen router and using DS-Lite
  • Rakuten Hikari DS-Lite is Xpass

GT7 (RMX6688) Port Package AOD Fix / Backup Work Log

Device: realme GT7 China hardware RMX6688 (project number 24618), serial number 3B1F5TE6K0YF1PRM, rooted (KernelSU).
Flashed with a port package: International version RMX5061 EX01 → China hardware.

Iron rule: Not a bit of data may be lost. Only read-only operations are performed on the phone. fastboot flash/erase/format/-w/set_active, setprop/resetprop persist, rm or writes to /data, and factory reset must each first obtain the user’s explicit consent. Before flashing, the backup must first pass verification and have already been copied to a second disk.

1. Current version composition of the phone (verified 2026-10-11)

LayerVersion
Upper layer (system / product, etc.)International version MY 593, fingerprint oplus/ossi/ossi:15/AP3A.240617.008/1755013304553
my_manifestChina 802: RMX6688_15.0.1.802(CN01), ota RMX6688_11.A.38_0380_202509082012
Lower layer (vendor)China A.01, realme/RMX6688/RE602AL1…
tee_bChina 802
init_bootKernelSU patched version
vbmetaflags=3 (verification disabled, at offset 123 bytes)
  • A/B partitions plus Virtual A/B, current slot is b.
  • The international version has no 802 base package, so the port package uses the China package for the lower layer.
  • Do not use system OTA updates: my_manifest is China 802, so a China OTA might be pushed. This is an inference, not actually tested.

2. AOD Fix (completed, user has confirmed fixed)

  • Root cause: display_features.xml in the port package’s my_product came from International version 24749 (oha_support / fingeprint_optical_enabled). The fix was to replace it with the China 24618 configuration and remove disable_aod_all_day_mode.
  • Flashing: 2026-10-10, under fastbootd only my_product_b was flashed, image was my_product_B_allday.img (md5 3916e32a6e9e9cbb14165ae22b4f4894, 2557247488 B). This flash was approved by the user (“I agree that you can start flashing”), and the consent is valid only for this one time.
  • fastbootd driver: Requires Google USB driver (VID_18D1&PID_4EE0), r13 version, installed on this computer with pnputil /add-driver … /install.
  • Image location (the original F:\tmp\gt7aod\out has been deleted): O:\GT7_backup_20261010_copy\aod_fix\
    • my_product_B_allday.img: md5 3916e32a…, this is what is currently on the phone.
    • my_product_A_cn_exact.img: md5 39d437f5…, alternative plan A.
    • my_product_ORIGINAL_rollback.img: md5 6ef16441…, 2533498880 B, for rollback.
  • If the port package (flash.bat) is flashed again in the future, it will overwrite my_product back to the old version, and the B version image will need to be flashed again.

3. Backup

Partitions + mounted partitions (completed and verified)

  • C:\Users\Wray\GT7_backup_20261010\
    • partitions\: 103 physical partitions plus super.img, all compared with sha256 on the phone. In partitions\SHA256SUMS, nvdata appears on two lines; the last line ffd951a8… is authoritative.
    • Also logical\, mounted\, super_chunks\, _incomplete\.
    • data_ps1\: tar archives of mounted partitions have been verified; internal storage was only partially backed up, because the adb service disconnected midway and Android.tar was truncated.
    • data_full\: left over from an interrupted test on 2026-10-11, about 392MB, incomplete, can be deleted.
    • data\: empty directory.
  • Copy on the second disk: O:\GT7_backup_20261010_copy\, 124 files verified, also contains aod_fix\ and SHA256SUMS_copy.txt.
  • O:\DNA3-36-win\GT7_backup_20261010\: only text lists and a few directories, an early artifact.
  • User data (internal storage about 33GB, app data 65GB or more): the user said it had already been backed up before, so no full backup was made this time.

7z archives (in O:\DNA3-36-win\)

FileDescription
Realme GT7 For_EX01.7zOriginal port package, untouched
Realme GT7 For_EX01_本机一致版.7z7742841918 B, tested with 7zr t and CRC compared. Consistent with the phone’s current state: my_product is the fixed version, flash.bat has added my_company_a / my_manifest_a, tee is 802, init_boot is KernelSU, with init_boot_stock_A01.img and 修改说明.txt also attached. The positions recorded with lpdump were used to slice out each logical partition from super for comparison; the flash targets match slot b (except for vbmeta’s flag).
GT7_本机专属分区_3B1F5TE6K0YF1PRM_20261010.7z118514412 B, verified. Contains 22 device-specific partition images: nvdata, nvcfg, nvram, protect1/2, md_sec, persist, proinfo, seccfg, sec1, otp, oplusreserve1/2/3/5/6, metadata, para, boot_para, dram_para, expdb, frp; also tar archives of 5 mounted partitions, 说明.txt, SHA256SUMS.txt, getprop, by-name. Can only be flashed back to this phone.
Realme GT7 For_EX01_AOD修复版.7zHas been replaced by the device-consistent version and is no longer in the directory (user deleted it).
  • tee is not different for every machine: the tee image is vendor-signed generic firmware. Each machine’s own keys and data are in partitions such as nvdata, protect, and md_sec (included in the device-specific package above).

4. General-purpose backup scripts

O:\DNA3-36-win\Android_full_backup.ps1 (PowerShell 5.1 / 7, UTF-8 BOM, CRLF)

  • Backup content:
    • When rooted: dd physical partitions (excluding userdata, swap, whole-disk devices, and duplicate devices); logical partitions are exported separately only when -AllLogical or -Only is added; writable mounted partitions are tarred; internal storage; app data under /data (split by app).
    • When not rooted: only backs up /sdcard and third-party app apks.
  • Verification method:
    • Partitions are compared with sha256 against the phone side; when a partition is being written by the system, the result of two consecutive identical reads is used.
    • Large partitions are read in chunks and can resume after interruption.
    • tar archives are compared by file count and byte count; hard links are counted only once by inode.
    • A tar archive must end with two all-zero blocks; otherwise it is considered incomplete.
  • Read-only guarantee: All commands sent to the phone go through a read-only check. Commands are first base64-encoded, then passed through adb exec-out "echo <b64>|base64 -d|su".
  • Issues fixed on 2026-10-11 according to review comments:
    • The read-only check mismatched quotes when encountering '\'' escapes.
    • On adb transfer errors, it now checks the exit code and stderr and retries; after consecutive failures it stops, and rerunning can resume.
    • In -Live mode, if the phone has files but the archive has none, it is no longer accepted.
    • When file names differ only by case, a hash is uniformly added to distinguish them (Clash).
    • Hard link deduplication.
    • Internal storage is all handled as -Live.
    • SHA256SUMS and logs changed to no BOM.
    • Free space check under network paths (UNC).
    • Wait-Device displays adb’s actual state.
    • In the non-root path, the package name of pm path has escaping added.
  • Real-device tests (read-only, -Only misc,frp,persist,nvdata,metadata) all passed.

O:\DNA3-36-win\android_full_backup.py (Python 3.8+, standard library only, cross-platform, LF, no BOM)

  • Functionally equivalent to the ps1. Output directory, file names, .ok markers, and SHA256SUMS are completely identical, and the two scripts can resume each other’s backups.
  • tar verification now uses Python’s tarfile; the RHT.security.selinux pax records generated by toybox can be parsed normally.
  • Porting process: 1 agent implemented, 3 reviewed by direction, 1 fixed, 1 offline tested, all using the default model. The review raised 11 issues, 9 were fixed. The two not changed: one is the tie order in partition sorting, which does not affect the result; the other is the way Clash is determined — actual testing showed that PowerShell hashtables are inherently case-insensitive, and the current implementation behaves the same as the ps1.
  • Offline tests were run with a fake adb and all passed: full backup, rerun skip, --only, non-root, transfer failure retry, truncated tar rejected, partition content changing during read, various special file names, hard links, read-only check.
  • Real-device tests (read-only, same set of partitions) passed. The hashes of misc, frp, and metadata are the same as in the ps1 run; nvdata and persist are written during runtime, so differing between the two runs is normal.
  • Incident record: The implementing agent once ran the script without adding the --adb parameter and connected to the real phone. Only read-only commands were executed (get-state, getprop, cat /proc/mounts, cat /proc/partitions, lpdump); there was no dd and no writing of any kind; the temporary text generated was deleted. The user was truthfully informed.
  • Note: The previously used Python virtual environment F:\tmp\gt7aod\venv was deleted along with tmp; from now on it needs to be run with the system Python.

5. Pitfalls encountered

  • adb stderr under PS 5.1: At ErrorActionPreference=Stop, it is treated as NativeCommandError, and needs to be changed locally to Continue.
  • Multiline here-string in CRLF scripts: \r must be removed before sending to the phone.
  • Checking with bsdtar after packing with toybox: The pax record written by tar --selinux has a trailing NUL, and bsdtar reports “malformed pax attributes”, but the content is intact. To determine whether an archive is complete, look at the two all-zero blocks at the end.
  • The adb service disconnecting midway truncates the tar: This is why transfer checks were added.
  • fastbootd cannot detect the phone: The Google USB driver needs to be installed.
  • Flashing a larger image: Logical partitions automatically expand.
  • Workflow scripts must not contain CR: Write with LF; a single agent’s output must be length-limited, otherwise it will exceed the 32k output limit.
  • Claude Pro quota: No more than 3 top-tier models running in parallel at the same time.

6. To-do / Optional

  • Delete C:\Users\Wray\GT7_backup_20261010\data_full (leftover from the interrupted test), pending the user’s decision.
  • If a complete user data backup is needed in the future, use either script with --no-partitions / -NoPartitions, and confirm the phone is unlocked before backing up.

Windows Mapped Drives to Achieve Linux-like Management

Registry subst+link

Ultimate Implementation Plan: Perform Global Mapping via the SYSTEM Account

Registry Execution

Windows’ kernel (Session Manager), at boot time, does read a specific registry path as SYSTEM to load drives. This is the DOS Devices we mentioned earlier.

  • The /v value must include a colon: it must be D:, not D.

  • The /d data must include the kernel escape prefix: it must be \??\C:\your_folder. Here, \??\ tells the Windows Object Manager that this is a direct local file system parse request.

After modification, remember to configure ACLs to avoid occasional permission issues.

icacls "C:\Tools" /grant:r "$($env:USERNAME):(OI)(CI)F" /T /C

Manual

We need to use “Task Scheduler” to have the system, at startup or user logon, use the identity of SYSTEM to silently execute subst.

Steps:

  1. Clean up remnants: First, execute subst D: /D in all terminals, and delete the previously tested registry mappings and SMB mappings to ensure the D drive is completely freed.
  2. Open Task Scheduler: Press Win + R, type taskschd.msc, and press Enter.
  3. Create the core task: In the right-hand Actions pane, click “Create Task…” (note: not “Create Basic Task”).
  4. Configure the [General] tab:
    • Name: enter any name, for example Global_Subst_D
    • Security options: click “Change User or Group” -> enter SYSTEM -> click “Check Names” (it will become NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM) -> OK.
    • Check “Run with highest privileges” at the bottom.
  5. Configure the [Triggers] tab:
    • Click “New…”.
    • Begin the task: select “At log on”.
    • Settings: select “Any user”.
    • Click OK.
  6. Configure the [Actions] tab (key):
    • Click “New…”.
    • Action: select “Start a program”.
    • Program/script: enter cmd.exe
    • Add arguments: enter /c subst D: C:\cuda (replace C:\cuda with your actual deep directory path)
    • Click OK.
  7. Configure the [Conditions] tab:
    • Uncheck “Start the task only if the computer is on AC power” (to prevent it from failing when a laptop is on battery).
  8. Save and apply immediately:
    • Click “OK” to save the task.
    • In the task list, find the Global_Subst_D you just created, right-click it, and select “Run”.

OpenWrt

Export All Packages

Hardware Acceleration

firewall

Select hardware acceleration enabled

wed

Check cat /sys/kernel/debug/mt76/mt7915/wed_mode

Scheduled Reboot

* * * * * sleep 70 && touch /etc/banner && reboot

sleep 70 Avoid repeated reboots due to identical timestamp verification after reboot

touch /etc/banner Clear login records, and at the same time touch to avoid the router not doing NTP in time causing time verification; set the router time to the time at reboot, touch file makes the time after reboot (before NTP) the last modification time of the file

LuCI Crash

Caused by uhttpd

dnsmasq Forwarding

No Network After Reboot

On some specific CPU architectures (such as some MediaTek, Realtek solutions, or old x86 NICs), OpenWrt’s open-source drivers are not perfect. During a system soft reboot, it fails to successfully send a reset instruction to the NIC chip

2.5G Interface Failure (rtl822x)

Interface deadlock caused by unstable driver, needs to be reloaded

ipv6 nat

Interface Reboot

Commonly used when zetotier and other intranet penetration/tunneling are unreachable (slow WAN port startup)

/etc/hotplug.d/iface/99-zerotier

Interface Traffic Splitting

MWAN3

Disable all hardware acceleration, firewall & wed

Because of public network traversal, for IPv6 it is best not to use load balancing when not using NAT6

  1. Register Interfaces: Register all interfaces you want to split traffic across

  2. Add Members: Create MWAN interfaces, set metric (priority), weight (traffic ratio)

  3. Set Policies: Bundle the required members (that need to be split together) into one policy. For public network allocation, a separate policy needs to be set here

  4. Set Rules: Destination address 0.0.0.0/0, i.e., split all external network IPs. For public network allocation, source address filtering needs to be set here.

Rules ultimately determine the effect. If you need to test, create a policy bound to a single interface and create a rule moved to the top

Test interface: mwan3 use {interface} curl api.ipify.org

Manual Configuration

Preserve External Access

Create a routing table (if registering a name, it needs to be written to a file)

echo "101 pppoe" >> /etc/iproute2/rt_tables

/etc/nftables.d/99-pppoe-mark.nft

/etc/hotplug.d/iface/99-pppoe-policy-route

Block IP

Directly binding an interface will cause other tunneling interfaces to malfunction

bash scripts

on

off

ipv6 Multi-WAN Configuration

v4

* * * * * /root/failover.sh

v6

* * * * * /root/failover_v6.sh

Public Network Access

Configure inbound for the router’s own services in traffic rules

Configure forwarding for services within the subnet in port forwarding

For subnet public IPv6 to be accessed externally, configure traffic rules

Assign Public IPv6 to Subnet (only needed in /64 PD case)

/64 is the smallest physical broadcast domain (subnet), i.e., /64 should be treated as network nodes communicating directly (responding to NDP, same link on-link), so an NDP proxy is needed

/60 /56 and larger ranges can be routed by default and can be forwarded

Forwarding state next-hop and endpoint state on-link

Enable DHCP server on wan6: enable the specified main interface, change RA, DHCP, and NDP all to relay

LAN v6 configuration: change RA, DHCP, and NDP all to relay

If using only one public IPv6, enable IPv6 masquerading (NAT66) in advanced settings under firewall WAN

Route Tracing

Configuration Lost After Running for a While

The cause is that f2fs journal mode is incompatible with the router

TTL boot, press f and Enter to enter fix mode

This bug is caused by 2.5G initialization of the chip

May cause overview not to display, use the following alternatives

  • luci-mod-dashboard
  • luci-app-statistics

After restoring the backup file, you need to reset SSH to update the key for public network access

No Network After Reboot

Use reboot -f to reboot

Processor energy performance
Processor performance core parking minimum cores
Link State Power Management
USB selective suspend

Only Enable Commonly Used Settings

Processor performance boost mode be337238-...
This is the most critical one; it’s not overclocking, it manages the Turbo Boost policy:

ValueModeEffect
0DisabledNo Turbo Boost, locks the base frequency, coolest and most power-efficient
1EnabledStandard Turbo Boost, speeds up only when needed
2AggressiveRamps Turbo Boost to maximum whenever there is any load
3Efficient EnabledWill Turbo Boost but prioritizes power saving
4Efficient AggressiveTurbo Boosts as much as possible while saving power
5/6At GuaranteedVersions that provide additional precise speed boosts above the guaranteed base frequency

Processor energy efficiency preference 36687f9e-...
A 0-100 slider, 0 = performance, 100 = power saving. Directly determines how aggressive the CPU is.

Core parking 0cc5b647... minimum / ea062031... maximum
Fill in a percentage. 100 = never park, lowest latency; 0 = park freely, saves power but switching programs may briefly stutter.

Console lock display off timeout 8EC4B3A5... / Unattended sleep timeout 7bc4a2f9...
These two are Windows’ most troublesome hidden settings. Even if you set it to never sleep, the screen still goes black and sleeps after 2 minutes on the lock screen; it’s System unattended sleep timeout defaulting to 120 seconds that’s causing the problem.

AHCI HIPM/DIPM 0b2d69d7...
0 = Active fastest, 1 = HIPM, 2 = DIPM, 3 = HIPM+DIPM, 4 = Lowest most power-saving. Only effective for SATA SSD/HDD.
